title: Maintaining Proper Drain Pipe Slope for Long-Term Flow
description: Proper pipe slope is essential for self-scouring drainage lines. If a horizontal drain pipe has insufficient slope, waste solids settle at the bottom, leading to frequent blockages over time. Conversely, excessive pitch can allow liquids to flow past solids without carrying them along. During routine maintenance inspections, checking pipe hangers and supports ensures that lines do not sag or lose pitch over time. Maintaining uniform slope prevents standing water pockets, reduces sludge accumulation, and extends the life of the DWV system.

Maintaining Proper Drain Pipe Slope for Long-Term Flow

Proper pipe slope is essential for self-scouring drainage lines. If a horizontal drain pipe has insufficient slope, waste solids settle at the bottom, leading to frequent blockages over time. Conversely, excessive pitch can allow liquids to flow past solids without carrying them along. During routine maintenance inspections, checking pipe hangers and supports ensures that lines do not sag or lose pitch over time. Maintaining uniform slope prevents standing water pockets, reduces sludge accumulation, and extends the life of the DWV system.
